tier1.name: Functional / Stress Hardening
reportedRegressionRequirements: Game Center selected event follows the active game video on direct tune, Next, and automatic advance
Background program refresh cannot replace or restart the active media key
Manual pause remains latched for at least 25 seconds under background refresh
Score-ribbon date browsing cannot autoplay Silver daily/weekly roundup media
Production startup contains no legacy NBA/demo seed programming
Post-first-frame playback buffering self-recovers by failing over within a bounded window instead of hanging or restarting the same clip
Launch-started YouTube media enters a tracked playback session immediately and cannot remain indefinitely in starting while iframe readiness never arrives
Every clean-window error capable of blocking certification is exported with timestamp, category/code, source, message, detail/data, and browser/runtime identity
A count-only clean-window error with no corresponding exported error record cannot independently fail Tier 1; the diagnostic mismatch remains visible as an advisory

Known transient browser media interruptions are advisory only when a later PASS playback step plus a final PLAYING/OK playback session prove automatic recovery and are labeled RECOVERED_ADVISORY in the exported certificate

Post-test exact-state restoration is advisory unless final application health is bad; cleanup health requires restored resource mode, playback ownership OK, one soundtrack audio element, a selected media item on a started board, and Game Center consistency for game-scoped media
Playback watchdog failures that prove bounded automatic failover to a different PLAYING media asset and healthy post-test state are RECOVERED_ADVISORY rather than Tier 1 blockers.

Poisoned media is blocked before native/YouTube player assignment; any already-loading matching resources are torn down locally without resetting the healthy playback engine, and certification requires zero orphaned blocked loads.
Recap tier availability is keyed to physical playback identity: the same YouTube ID/direct URL cannot be advertised as both Green Quick and Purple Extended.
Known physical duration outranks conflicting discovery-objective metadata when assigning Quick versus Extended recap tiers.

Recent NFL weekly recap playlists are dynamically discovered from the official NFL YouTube channel; missing expected preseason/regular-season week catalogs trigger a bounded refresh instead of waiting on the long-lived playlist cache.
Custom competition creation is Dev Mode only and persists server-side.
Active special events appear in both Special Events and the main selector row; completed special events remain only under Special Events.
Custom event Game Center uses the canonical /api/events/<competition>/<event>/game-center contract.
World Cup and LLWS templates require schedule review before activation.
Competition Builder editable controls isolate keyboard input from document-level playback shortcuts so typing spaces/arrows cannot control playback.
Competition creation is not reported successful until the shared server store is written and a fresh definition read-back verifies persistence.
Custom competitions are enrolled in the canonical history league registry, operator playlist crawler, and dedicated background media gap-search worker.
Schedule Auto Discover uses structured output and falls back to direct extraction of an operator-supplied official schedule URL when web search fails.

Competition Builder schedule discovery is completeness-driven: large tournaments are researched in bounded date windows, merged/deduplicated, and checked against an expected event count instead of relying on one giant model response.
Site-wide competition creation rejects zero-event schedules and rejects incomplete schedules when an expected event count is known unless a future explicit override is introduced.

Dev Mode can delete a custom competition site-wide, removing its persisted definition, history event relationships, operator playlist registrations, runtime registry entry, and history-league crawl enrollment.
World Cup and LLWS templates carry deterministic completeness targets of 104 and 38 competition games respectively.
Special Events is a permanent top-level selector control; custom special-event catalog refreshes populate that stable control instead of transiently injecting/removing the control itself.
Selecting a completed or upcoming special event while browsing outside its event date range navigates the score ribbon into the event range before rendering its games.
Custom competition score hydration subscribes to the canonical ScoreDateStore browse-date authority so special-event games render on historical event dates across normal ribbon refreshes.
Special Events dropdown content is rendered in a viewport-level portal so the horizontally scrolling league-filter container cannot clip its menu.
Custom competition date hydration rebuilds the verified-media lookup used by score-card playback after schedule/media enter ScoreDateStore.
Custom operator playlist registrations are durably saved before asynchronous playlist crawl begins; existing custom competitions re-enroll media sources on server startup.
Custom event-media responses force canonical competition/event identity from the event relationship and lazily repair matching unassigned custom source media.
Competition Builder persists an explicit participant artwork strategy; the FIFA World Cup defaults to country flags while future competitions can choose team logos, provided artwork, auto, or none.
Competition Builder startup cannot recursively resolve the Special Events portal; the stable Special Events menu is read from the application DOM and may then be portaled to the viewport.
Competition Builder startup exposes READY/ERROR boot state and surfaces a visible Special Events warning if initialization fails instead of silently removing all custom-competition UI.
The 4.6.4 custom competition runtime bridge, participant artwork strategy, canonical custom-media identity repair, and verified-media lookup rebuild remain required in 4.6.6.

Special-event main-row eligibility is evaluated against the score ribbon browse date, so a historical tournament is treated as an active league while browsing dates inside its event window even after the real-world event has completed.
Special Events dropdown presentation does not expose internal event-count bookkeeping and instead presents a clean event identity plus date-relative active/completed status.

Past tournament bracket placeholders are reconciled to actual played participants/results from authoritative sources while preserving each canonical event ID so existing media associations remain intact.
Custom competition playback exposes explicit away/home display-name strings alongside rich participant objects and artwork so legacy title paths cannot render [object Object].
Participant artwork strategy is preserved through custom schedule hydration and Game Center; the FIFA World Cup AUTO/template strategy resolves country participants to flag artwork.
Tournament ingestion is state-aware: matches dated today or earlier use actual realized participants/results, while future bracket placeholders remain only until official participants are determined.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup uses ESPN fifa.world as the deterministic primary participant/result authority.
Provider match IDs are stored separately while canonical Sports Big Board event IDs remain unchanged.
Ongoing tournaments resolve future bracket slots as soon as both actual participants are officially known.
Custom soccer competitions use the standard ESPN soccer Game Center structure with scoring plays, team stats, player/lineup sections, commentary timeline, venue/status and soccer completeness rules.
If ESPN soccer Game Center cannot be loaded, the generic custom Game Center remains a non-breaking fallback.
History Audit exposes a Statistics tab with per-competition game/media coverage and includes dynamically registered special events.
Media Playlists dynamically exposes registered special-event competitions alongside MLB, NFL, NBA, NHL, EPL, and MLS.
Every competition can explicitly reprocess media from the Media Playlists or Statistics surfaces without deleting existing verified media.
Built-in league media reprocessing reopens the normal source-enrichment ledger so completed source checks become eligible again.
Special-event media reprocessing force-crawls every enabled operator playlist and runs canonical event-media association repair.
When tournament participant/result reconciliation changes an event from bracket identity to realized teams, registered competition playlists are force-crawled again automatically.
History Audit, Silver, playlist-management, and recovery league selectors are populated from the live competition/media registry rather than a six-league hard-coded list.
Completed custom soccer events normalize provider terminal states such as FT to canonical FINAL before score-ribbon playback eligibility is evaluated.
A past custom soccer event with official scores cannot remain canonically SCHEDULED; it is exposed as FINAL while preserving the provider status separately.
Future and live custom soccer matches are never forced to FINAL merely because a score is present.
World Cup verified GAME media associated to a completed match remains eligible for the normal score-ribbon play arrow and click-to-play path.
Existing persisted World Cup FT/stale-completion rows are normalized on schedule reads and revisited by background result reconciliation without changing canonical event IDs.
Historical score-ribbon dates remain database-first: FIND RECAP and external discovery are gated until normalized catalog hydration and date-scoped association repair complete.
Historical ribbon reads re-prove already-downloaded orphaned or quarantined GAME assets against the requested date before external media discovery begins.

Schedule/provider event-id changes that are proven to be the same league/date/team/time matchup are stored as aliases to the existing canonical event instead of breaking historical media relationships.
Bulk historical ribbon media is exposed under canonical event keys and all proven provider aliases while the underlying source-to-game relationship remains singular.
Historical date switching is generation-safe: a late database hydration from a previously browsed date cannot launch recap search or repaint the current date.
Historical diagnostics distinguish database association readiness from genuine no-media state and report games checked, ribbon-ready games, and remaining missing games.
Competition Builder Identity exposes an Event Icon selector beside Sport with a prepopulated reusable icon library.
eventIcon is persisted as competition metadata and each Special Events dropdown row renders that event-specific icon with a sport-aware fallback for older competitions.

The 2026 Little League Baseball World Series template remains completeness-gated at 38 competition games, uses August 19-30, 2026, and points schedule discovery at the official Little League tournament schedule.
The LLWS template defaults to baseball, the baseball event icon, ESPN league slug llb, provider sport baseball, and the standard baseball Game Center profile.

2026 LLWS played games use ESPN baseball/llb as a deterministic participant/result authority while canonical Sports Big Board event IDs remain stable and unresolved future bracket participants remain placeholders only until official.

Custom baseball special events with an ESPN provider mapping use the standard baseball Game Center structure including inning linescore, team stats, player sections, timeline/scoring plays when provided, with the generic custom Game Center retained as a non-breaking fallback.

LLWS automatically inherits special-event playlist enrollment, Statistics reporting, media reprocessing, historical database-first hydration, schedule aliases, and date-scoped media reassociation from the existing generic competition contracts.
Competition Builder exposes a COPY TEMPLATE JSON control that copies the canonical generic special-event schedule import structure without generating Sports Big Board event IDs.

The generic schedule import structure supports rich away/home participant objects with name, displayName, group, abbreviation, and aliases plus scheduledAt, scores, provider IDs, gameNumber, round/stage, venue, city/country, and sourceUrl.
Custom competition media sources can persist optional required/excluded playlist title phrases; required phrases are OR-based and any excluded phrase rejects the candidate before GAME association.

Historical Database Game Media Playlists exposes the same required/excluded playlist title phrases for existing special-event sources and rule changes trigger a force recrawl without deleting existing source media.
Custom-event media association uses imported participant aliases, abbreviations, groups, and region identities as additional event-match evidence while preserving canonical event IDs.
LLWS template media matching defaults the Green source required phrase to Full Game Highlights while remaining operator-editable and reusable for other competitions.
Special-event operator playlist association compares every title-rule-eligible GAME asset against the full competition schedule before publication date can narrow candidates.
Required/excluded playlist title phrases are evaluated before tournament-wide event association so miscellaneous clips remain SOURCE_MEDIA and do not compete with configured game recaps.
Participant names, aliases, abbreviations, groups, and regions remain valid matchup evidence across the full competition candidate set.

Repeated participant matchups are resolved only by stronger provider identity, explicit title game number/date, or bounded publication-date proximity; unresolved ambiguity remains orphaned rather than guessed.
Already-downloaded special-event operator playlist orphans are re-associated from SOURCE_MEDIA at backend startup without redownloading or deleting source assets.
Future special-event playlist crawls persist both the internal operator playlist ID and provider YouTube playlist ID so multi-playlist title rules remain deterministic.
Special-event Statistics WITH MEDIA uses durable playable EVENT_MEDIA relationships that the score ribbon can actually consume instead of broad source-catalog availability.
REPROCESS MEDIA uses the tournament-wide special-event crawler so orphan counts and ribbon-ready game coverage converge on the same durable association truth.
Special-event media association derives media-facing geographic identities from imported participant aliases, including the final state/country component of City, State/Country location aliases.
Imported participant group labels ending in Region contribute a media alias without the Region suffix while one-character abbreviations are excluded from title matching.

Special-event media titles containing public state/country identities such as Alabama, Ohio, Washington, Nicaragua, Czechia, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Iowa can match the canonical schedule participant objects without rewriting those schedule objects.
Common recap abbreviations and equivalents such as PA/NJ, DR/Dominican Republic, Curacao/Curaçao, and Czechia/Czech Republic are normalized as media aliases.
The special-event tournament crawler attempts a deterministic two-sided SPECIAL_EVENT_TITLE_ALIAS_PAIR match before falling back to the generic event matcher.
Existing special-event SOURCE_MEDIA orphans are automatically re-associated after the v4.6.14 media-alias layer installs; canonical event IDs and existing EVENT_MEDIA remain unchanged.

Persistence accepts a deterministic special-event proof only when it is produced by the internal SBB special-event matcher, names the exact target league/event/canonical key, carries both title-side aliases, and has confidence of at least 0.90.
A SPECIAL_EVENT_TITLE_ALIAS_PAIR proof is not reinterpreted by the older canonical-team-only event matcher during the same put_event_media write.
Existing TITLE_TEAM_PAIR_CONFLICT quarantines can be released to ASSIGNED only after the exact special-event alias proof is re-established for the same canonical event.
A pre-proven special-event asset never steals an asset that is already ASSIGNED to another canonical event; the new candidate remains MULTI_EVENT_CANDIDATE_ENCOUNTER.
Ordinary built-in league and generic event-media persistence continues to use the original fail-closed event matcher with no bypass.
Relationship repair may run the normal generic revalidation, but still-valid persisted internal special-event proofs are restored before repair completes.
v4.6.15 automatically re-associates existing special-event SOURCE_MEDIA after installation so previously quarantined Full Game Highlights do not require playlist deletion or redownload.

Pre-proven special-event persistence creates or refreshes the canonical-event parent and validates both canonical-event and source-media foreign-key parents on the same SQLite transaction before writing history_event_media.
Special-event media association is consolidated into an explicit SOURCE -> ELIGIBLE -> CANDIDATES -> MATCHED -> PERSISTED -> PLAYABLE pipeline with per-asset audit output.

For custom competitions, the persistent custom-competition registry event is the participant-identity authority; normalized history/provider refreshes may update runtime metadata but may not erase imported aliases, groups, abbreviations, or official gameNumber.
Special-event participant crosswalks derive stable media-facing identities from imported team names, aliases, locations, groups, regions, and safe abbreviations before media association.
Special-event association prefers a unique official gameNumber when media names one, then evaluates the full tournament using participant alias pairs and deterministic repeated-matchup tie breakers.
REASSOCIATE is database-only and never revisits a provider; RECRAWL SOURCES is the only operator action that performs provider/network collection before reassociation.
Association Audit exposes every source asset's eligibility result, candidate count, selected canonical event, association method, persistence state, playability, and rejection reason.

Once a special-event media asset is durably assigned, its normalized source scope is GAME with SPECIAL_EVENT_CANONICAL_ASSOCIATION so Statistics and historical ribbon playback read the same EVENT_MEDIA truth.
Special-event WITH MEDIA means at least one durable playable assigned EVENT_MEDIA relationship, never merely a source candidate or broad catalog match.

v4.6.16 migrates LLWS2026 to two explicit sources without recreating the schedule: LittleLeague.org Game Recaps as Green and the ESPN 2026 LLWS YouTube playlist as Purple with Full Game Highlights title eligibility.

The WEB_RECAP_INDEX source adapter collects only Recap: video pages, preserves LittleLeague.org as the official external source, promotes direct MP4/HLS media when exposed, and records Brightcove embed metadata when direct media is not available.

For special events, custom-competition registry events are the identity authority; provider/history rows may enrich runtime metadata but cannot replace imported participant aliases, groups, abbreviations, or official gameNumber.

Once v4.6.16 proves a special-event title by official gameNumber or a deterministic two-sided participant-alias pair, persistence writes the normalized history_event_media relationship directly and does not run the legacy canonical-team-only matcher a second time.

LLWS source migration re-reads the full persisted competition definition after save_competition because catalog rows intentionally omit events; startup reassociation therefore always retains the imported identity crosswalk.
LittleLeague.org recap pages preserve publication metadata when available so repeated participant matchups can use the same bounded chronology tie-breaker as YouTube playlist media.
Special-event orphan counts mean SOURCE_MEDIA assets with no durable ASSIGNED EVENT_MEDIA relationship; playable coverage is reported separately from association coverage.
If both event-family and collection-family integrity drift are present, startup repair forces both families before the hard post-repair audit.
The v4.6.16 relationship-routing correction installs synchronously during sbb import so it is active before server.py executes the backend startup repair gate.

Competition Registry 2.0 is the backend authority for competition existence and retains the COMPETITIONS mutable-mapping, catalog(), and enabled_ids() compatibility contracts used by server.py and Competition Builder.

Built-in leagues and dynamically-created leagues/special events share the same observable CompetitionCatalog; direct COMPETITIONS[id] registration emits REGISTER/UPDATE events and deletion emits UNREGISTER.
A dynamically-created competition is automatically enrolled in HISTORY_LEAGUES and Day State through registry events without a hard-coded league branch or backend redeploy.

Day State Engine persists precomputed day snapshots in day-state.sqlite3 and projects the existing canonical _history_day_score_rows, _history_day_ribbon_plans, and _history_day_score_inventory_complete outputs instead of introducing a second scoring/media truth.

The existing /api/history/ribbon contract is served cache-first from Day State using scoreRowsByLeague and eventPlans, so the main Big Board reads a precomputed backend read model while retaining the previous handler as failure fallback.
Day State continuously warms today and nearby dates, prioritizes operator/browser focus dates, and uses short freshness windows for current/live days with long historical freshness windows.
The browser prepaints selected dates from /api/day-state and ingests the same compact catalog plans used by established ribbon logic; legacy provider/date loaders remain recovery/freshness fallbacks.
Historical Database Audit exposes DAY STATE and BACKEND REGISTRY operator views showing snapshot freshness and whether dynamically-created competitions are enrolled in History and Day State.

Backend Registry and Day State state survive frontend reloads; dynamic competition definitions remain sourced from the persistent Competition Builder store and are replayed into Competition Registry 2.0 on backend startup.
Day State facts are derived from the same snapshot as ribbon scores/media, including game counts, live/final counts, playable-game counts, and represented competitions.

The catalog integrity metric silverGameLeaks means an ASSIGNED event-media relationship whose current normalized source scope is not GAME; it is an event-link integrity condition and remains owned by event relationship repair.
Special-event media code does not monkeypatch HistoryRepository.repair_relationships or override the core server startup repair-family plan.
A persisted pre-proven special-event relationship may be restored after relationship repair only when the source asset's current normalized scope is GAME.

If a newer media classifier changes a proof-bearing source asset from GAME to DAY_LEAGUE, WEEK_LEAGUE, ROUND_LEAGUE, or another collection scope, pre-proven restoration must not resurrect its quarantined event relationship.
Trusted special-event persistence checks the normalized source scope before writing an ASSIGNED event link and fails closed with NON_GAME_SCOPE_PREPROVEN_REJECTED when that scope is not GAME.
The consolidated v4.6.16 canonical special-event persistence path may explicitly persist a deterministically proven game asset as scope GAME with reason SPECIAL_EVENT_CANONICAL_ASSOCIATION.
Day State browser-facing GET requests are stale-while-revalidate and never synchronously build a snapshot on the HTTP request thread.
A completely cold Day State date returns COLD_WARMING immediately while the existing /api/history/ribbon handler remains the immediate fallback for first paint.
A stale Day State snapshot is served immediately as STALE_REFRESHING and its date is promoted to the front of the background build queue.
The browser bounds Day State prepaint latency and immediately invokes the established historical ribbon fallback on pending, timeout, or unavailable Day State.

Frontend Competition Projection merges Competition Builder catalog data, backend Competition Registry 2.0 data, and the last good browser projection so transient bootstrap failures cannot erase dynamic competitions.

Configured special events remain visible in the SPECIAL EVENTS selector even when the richer Competition Builder catalog is temporarily unavailable; registry-backed completed/upcoming events remain discoverable.
The Dev Competition Builder launcher retries against lazily-created Settings DOM instead of assuming its anchor exists during initial page startup.
The canonical frontend competition model consults Frontend Competition Projection as a dynamic-competition fallback while allowing the richer Competition Builder definition to override it.

Frontend Competition Projection must not attach a document-wide MutationObserver that calls render because registry rendering itself mutates Special Events DOM and can create an infinite observer/render loop.
Frontend Competition Projection special-event and dynamic-league rendering is idempotent: unchanged registry state does not rewrite the same menu/filter DOM on every polling interval.
Dev Competition Builder late-DOM recovery uses a narrow retry timer and does not require observing unrelated page mutations.
The launch screen and launchPlayBtn remain responsive while dynamic competition metadata initializes in the background.

Release-blocking verification is behavior- and architecture-contract based; historical tests may not block deployment solely because of release-specific CSS class names, exact SQL strings, private helper names, or superseded internal source markers.
Historical Python regression discovery remains available as a legacy-advisory diagnostic archive and does not block deployment when only archived implementation-pinning tests fail.

The stable tests/test_release_behavior_gate.py suite is the blocking Python release gate for launch responsiveness, non-blocking Day State, dynamic competition/Special Events projection, version handshake, and verification-script integrity.
Syntax, manifest, version, Foundation Certification, Ultimate Playback, JavaScript runtime/contract checks, shell syntax, workflow-chain checks, and Pages dry-build checks remain blocking.
Tests explicitly referenced by active release checkers remain blocking foundation contracts even when the broader historical Python regression archive is advisory.
The v4.4.6 tests.test_v446_historical_media_quarantine static recovery contract remains an explicit blocking VERIFY.sh command because check_ultimate_playback.py requires it.
Verification cleanup may move superseded implementation-pinning tests to advisory status but may not remove commands required by check_foundation_certification.py or check_ultimate_playback.py.

Efficiency Certification continuously measures browser API latency, concurrent duplicate requests, main-thread long tasks, DOM-node count, optional JavaScript heap use, and launch responsiveness with bounded telemetry buffers.
Dev mode exposes an EFFICIENCY CERTIFICATION card with RUN AUTO TEST, RUN HAMMER, COPY REPORT, and RESET controls.

The automated efficiency test is backend read-only, saves the active ribbon date and competition filter, exercises multiple dates and competitions, and restores the exact browsing state when complete.
Efficiency certification reports distribution metrics including ribbon p50/p95/max and API p50/p95/max so intermittent latency is visible instead of being hidden by a single average.
Day State cache response headers are recorded during efficiency runs so READY, STALE_REFRESHING, and COLD_WARMING behavior can be correlated with ribbon latency.
The automated efficiency test records request failures, concurrent duplicate requests, ribbon timeouts, long-task counts/max duration, DOM growth, optional heap growth, and state-restoration success.
Efficiency instrumentation may not install a document-wide MutationObserver and may not issue backend mutation requests.
tests/test_v473_efficiency_runtime.js is a blocking browser contract for the Efficiency Certification surface and non-destructive automation guarantees.
Request Broker is the single browser network arbitration layer for API GET traffic: concurrent identical GETs share one transport request and each consumer receives its own Response clone.

Request Broker normalizes cache-buster query parameters, provides short-TTL reuse for read-only registry/Day State/history endpoints, and never coalesces non-GET, Range, soundtrack-stream, export, or download requests.
Interactive date changes create a monotonically increasing generation and abort superseded date-scoped Day State/ribbon/roundup/discovery transport work.
Date Transition Coordinator bypasses the older Day State wrapper's dual-path behavior and invokes the app date setter with load:false so roundups cannot block score-ribbon first paint.
Day State is the primary first-paint source. The legacy historical ribbon loader is invoked only when no Day State payload is available for a historical date.
Roundups and discovery are background enrichment after first paint rather than prerequisites for changing the ribbon date.
Day State operator-view installation uses a narrow retry timer and may not install a document-wide MutationObserver.

Efficiency Certification consumes Request Broker network telemetry rather than wrapping window.fetch a second time, and distinguishes network requests, coalesced callers, cache hits, superseded aborts, and endpoint p95/max latency.
Efficiency Certification reports maximum network requests per date and the ten slowest API endpoint families so request storms and backend hotspots are directly attributable.
tests/test_v474_efficiency_remediation_runtime.js is a blocking browser contract for Request Broker, Date Transition Coordinator, non-blocking enrichment, and broker-native efficiency telemetry.

Enrichment Firewall classifies API reads into FIRST_PAINT, SHARED_STATE, ON_DEMAND, IDLE_ENRICHMENT, LIVE_PROVIDER, or NORMAL and defers expensive non-first-paint work during the active ribbon transition quiet window.

Competition Builder schedule/media, rapid-team-videos, historical discovery, historical roundups, historical soccer schedules, and background Game Center reads may not start transport work during the first-paint quiet window unless they are explicit operator/on-demand work.
Competition Registry and Competition Builder catalog are shared application state with longer Request Broker TTLs rather than five-second transport polling.

Competition Builder, builder overlays, durable association statistics, and special-event media audit are loaded by Operator Module Loader only when the user opens builder/operator surfaces; they are not normal Big Board startup modules.
Special Events remain available while operator modules are unloaded because Frontend Competition Projection and backend Competition Registry 2.0 remain the normal competition-existence path.
Date Transition Coordinator does not automatically launch historical discovery/media search after a ribbon change and clears a selected event that belongs to the prior date.
Day State first-paint transitions bypass the legacy historical-media barrier when load:false/dayStateFirstPaint is intentional, while explicit legacy loads retain the database-before-search barrier.
Day State serializes snapshot builds per date so a cold ribbon fallback and background prewarmer cannot perform the same canonical historical calculation twice.
Day State worker refreshes today on a timed cadence rather than pushing today to the front on every loop, allowing registered special-event prewarm dates to drain.
Registered SPECIAL_EVENT schedules enqueue all canonical event dates for Day State background prewarm; data-driven league schedules prewarm only the near-live window.
Completed historical Day State snapshots with complete score inventory have a 24-hour freshness window, while incomplete historical snapshots refresh sooner.
Efficiency Certification reports deferred enrichment, deferred abort/release counts, lazy/loaded operator state, and the Date Transition first-paint source.
tests/test_v475_enrichment_firewall_runtime.js is a blocking browser contract for lazy operator modules, Enrichment Firewall, canonical cold builds, and special-event Day State prewarming.

Future scheduled score-ribbon dates are valid navigation targets and may not be clamped to the current local date; the date picker and forward pager remain enabled so upcoming tournament games can be inspected.
An early launch bridge is attached when the launch button is parsed so the user's START action is captured before the legacy DOMContentLoaded launch wiring completes.
Ribbon Render Pipeline preserves the first synchronous render call but suppresses only immediate same-state duplicate renders inside one browser frame and records render duration/node telemetry.
Day State apply owns the normal Day State first-paint render; Date Transition Coordinator may not unconditionally issue a second render after a successful Day State payload.
Cold historical fallback retains one explicit ribbon render because no Day State apply occurred.
Request Broker attaches the active efficiency run id when network transport begins and carries that immutable attribution through finish/error/metadata events.
Efficiency Certification excludes network work that began before the active test run even if that request finishes during the run.

Efficiency Certification records launch parse time, launch-handler-ready time, Render Pipeline p95/max/count/coalescing, and Day State STORE_SCORE_ROWS, INGEST_MEDIA_PLANS, and APPLY_TOTAL phase latency.
tests/test_v476_render_pipeline_runtime.js is a blocking browser contract for future-date navigation, launch readiness, render coalescing, and start-time efficiency attribution.
Each score-ribbon date transition opens one Render Pipeline generation before shell/data work begins and releases exactly one canonical first-paint commit after Day State or fallback state is ready.
Render requests made by shell, Day State, historical compatibility, or other ribbon callers while the active date generation is held are coalesced instead of performing live DOM work independently.
The ribbon renderer stages score-card appendChild operations in a DocumentFragment and performs one live #scoreCells append commit per actual render.
Render Pipeline records card-build time, DOM-commit time, next-frame paint delay, generation-commit status, and render reason counts.
Day State apply requests a render from Render Pipeline instead of forcing a synchronous render while an active date generation is held.

Efficiency Certification uses first usable canonical score-card paint as the blocking ribbon performance metric; continued background refresh/full-settle state is reported separately and does not create a false first-paint timeout.
Future scheduled dates with visible scheduled game cards are first-paint complete even when Day State remains STALE_REFRESHING in the background.
Efficiency Certification reports first-paint p95/max/timeouts separately from full-settle p95/timeouts and reports CARD_BUILD_P95, DOM_COMMIT_P95, BROWSER_PAINT_P95, and RENDER_REASONS.

tests/test_v477_first_paint_render_consolidation_runtime.js is a blocking contract for generation-owned first paint, DocumentFragment ribbon commits, and first-paint-vs-settle certification semantics.

Day State merges future history_catalog_event schedule rows into scoreRowsByLeague before media plans and summary generation so future tournament dates render scheduled canonical games even when the legacy history-day score cache is empty.

A future Day State snapshot that contains fewer games than the canonical catalog proves for that date is narrowly rebuilt under the per-date build mutex and returned as FUTURE_CATALOG_REBUILT; normal current and historical reads remain nonblocking.
Day State exposes projectionDiagnostics with future, catalogCandidates, catalogAdded, rowsBefore, rowsAfter, and leaguesAdded so future schedule projection can be audited without inference.

Render-Local Card Model Cache memoizes scoreCardAvailability, scoreCardPlayableItems, externalMediaItemsForGame, and scoreFromMatch only for one actual ribbon render and resets all WeakMap caches immediately afterward.
Render Pipeline records per-render card-cache hits, misses, and helper execution time without changing generation-owned first-paint or DocumentFragment commit semantics.

Efficiency Certification reports Day State games/scheduled/catalog candidate/catalog-added counts on every tested date so a future-date failure immediately distinguishes backend projection from frontend rendering.
Efficiency Certification samples JS heap before the run and over a post-restore idle window; heap retention uses the minimum post-test sample rather than a single arbitrary V8 heap point.

Heap retention remains an optional diagnostic and cannot independently make an otherwise healthy AUTO run fail; DOM retention, first-paint latency, API health, and main-thread latency remain the primary blocking signals.

tests/test_v478_future_projection_card_cache_runtime.js and tests/test_v478_future_projection.py are blocking contracts for future canonical schedule projection, render-local card caching, and stabilized memory certification.

All competitions classified as SPECIAL_EVENT, including older cached rows identified by generic eventIcon plus bounded event dates, live only in the Special Events dropdown and may not render as permanent main-row league chips.

Special Events dropdown is a fixed high-z-index themed menu anchored to the Special Events control; its event items show icon, short/name text, lifecycle state, selected state, and route selection through Frontend Competition Projection.
Score date selection uses the Sports Big Board themed custom calendar popover anchored under the date control instead of relying on the browser-native date picker popup.
The hidden native scoreDatePicker remains a compatibility value holder only and is moved off-screen with pointer events disabled so browser calendar UI cannot appear in the middle of the page.

The custom date calendar supports previous/next month navigation, 42-day month grid, selected date, today state, Today action, Close action, outside-click dismissal, Escape dismissal, resize/scroll repositioning, and future/past dates.
Efficiency first-paint detection accepts any non-roundup score ribbon child with stable non-loading content, including scheduled/bracket compatibility score-button or score-cell cards.
AUTO efficiency certification performs ten real left-arrow date steps followed by ten real right-arrow date steps and verifies each expected date reaches usable first paint.

AUTO efficiency certification performs random-access calendar jumps to representative previous-year January, February, June, previous Thanksgiving, and current-year January and June dates when historical.

Historical navigation reports p95/max latency, timeouts, wrong-date results, maximum network requests per navigation, and individual left/right/calendar transition lines; timeout or wrong-date navigation is blocking.
Render-local card cache additionally memoizes scoreGameLookupKeys and scoreEventDate during a single ribbon render.

ScoreDateStore preserves valid future YYYY-MM-DD keys for browse date, match snapshots, media snapshots, loading state, and lookups; future scheduled dates may not be normalized back to today.

The Aug 30 class of future-schedule regression is fixed at the data-store boundary: Day State rows for a future date remain stored under that exact future date and are therefore available to scoreMatchesForDate and the standard ribbon renderer.
Interactive date navigation is Day State-only for first paint. Date Transition Coordinator may not call /api/history/ribbon or a legacy history-ribbon fallback when a Day State snapshot is cold.

A totally cold historical Day State request builds a score-only canonical snapshot from history_catalog_event without media plans, discovery, provider calls, roundups, or historical-media association before first paint.

Cold historical thin snapshots are produced before the selected date is focused into the background full-build queue so the worker cannot race the thin path and hold first paint behind a multi-second full build.
Cold thin snapshots are persisted briefly as COLD_THIN_CATALOG and replaced asynchronously by the focused full Day State build.

The Day State thinProbe query is a non-mutating certification path that measures the cold score-only catalog projection even when the ordinary date snapshot has already been warmed by an earlier test run.
Efficiency Certification treats any /api/history/ribbon request during an AUTO/HAMMER run as a blocking regression because interactive first paint no longer depends on that endpoint.
Efficiency Certification reports cold-history thin p95/max/failures and blocks on cold thin p95 above the defined failure threshold.

Main-thread certification normalizes long-task load by the number of navigation/filter actions using long tasks per 10 actions and long-task milliseconds per action while retaining longest single task as a blocking latency signal.

Render-local card helper profiling reports per-helper p95, hits, and misses so scoreCardAvailability, scoreCardPlayableItems, externalMediaItemsForGame, scoreFromMatch, scoreGameLookupKeys, and scoreEventDate can be optimized individually.

tests/test_v4710_cold_history_future_store_runtime.js and tests/test_v4710_cold_history_future_store.py are blocking contracts for future-date storage, Day State-only cold history, thin first paint, and normalized main-thread certification.
Cold-history certification uses the dedicated GET /api/day-state/thin route rather than a thinProbe query sharing the ordinary /api/day-state broker/cache identity.

The dedicated thin-probe route performs only canonical catalog score projection and status counting; it does not write Day State cache/store, enqueue focus work, build media plans, run discovery, or call providers.

Cold-history thin-probe failures report HTTP status, error code, exception type, backend message, browser elapsed time, and backend thinCatalogMs so certification failures are diagnosable rather than N/A.
A render-scoped Score-Card Availability Index is keyed by stable canonical game identity and is rebuilt for every actual ribbon render.
Explicit scheduled games and score-only COLD_THIN_CATALOG snapshots bypass broad media candidate scanning because media cannot be a first-paint dependency for those states.
Games already present in verifiedPlayableItemsForGame use that canonical verified set directly during the render instead of rescanning broad media collections.
Unknown, live, or otherwise unresolved games preserve the certified legacy scoreCardPlayableItems implementation as an explicit fallback.
Render Pipeline reports availability index build time, indexed/verified/scheduled/thin counts, fast-path hits, fallback count, and fallback execution time.
Efficiency Certification reports AVAIL_INDEX_P95, AVAIL_FALLBACK_P95, AVAIL_FAST, and AVAIL_FALLBACKS alongside per-helper profiling.
ScoreDateStore public module API remains version 1.0.
tests/test_v4711_availability_index_thin_probe_runtime.js and tests/test_v4711_availability_index_thin_probe.py are blocking contracts.

Native Transport Snapshot captures the browser fetch implementation before Request Broker installation; it is reserved for certification diagnostics while normal application traffic remains broker-owned.

Score-card render model uses canonical Day State eventPlans and catalogPlanForScoreGame as the primary completed-game media source.
A Day State event plan with a non-empty playable array bypasses broad media pool scanning and supplies those canonical playable assets directly to scoreCardPlayableItems for that render.
Render-model game matching is stable-key based and tolerates cloned match objects using event ids, scoreGameLookupKeys aliases, and date/team pair fallback.
Scheduled games and COLD_THIN_CATALOG rows remain no-media first-paint fast paths; session verified media remains a secondary fast path.

Unknown, live, unresolved, or plan-without-playable games retain the original certified scoreCardPlayableItems implementation as fallback; newly resolved fallback media is memoized only for the active render.
Render Pipeline emits performance-time start/end boundaries plus date, filter, Day State plan count, plan-playable count, session-verified count, fast hits, and fallback counts.

Efficiency Certification correlates PerformanceObserver long tasks against overlapping render intervals and reports the five longest tasks with date, render reason, render/build duration, plan/fast/fallback counts, and overlap.
Efficiency Certification reports AVAIL_PLANS, AVAIL_PLAN_PLAYABLE, AVAIL_SESSION_VERIFIED, native thin transport state, and preserves existing AVAIL_INDEX/AVAIL_FALLBACK telemetry.
ScoreDateStore public module API remains exactly version 1.0.

tests/test_v4712_day_state_render_model_runtime.js and tests/test_v4712_day_state_render_model.py are blocking contracts for native thin transport, Day State media render model, stable-key matching, legacy fallback, and long-task attribution.
Efficiency Certification measures DAY_VISIBLE and MEDIA_READY as separate clocks for every representative date.
DAY_VISIBLE remains the first usable score-ribbon paint and is not delayed by media discovery or playback preparation.

MEDIA_READY is measured against games with already-known playable media in the authoritative score-card availability model, including canonical Day State plans and already-verified session media; genuinely missing media and background discovery do not hold date navigation open.

Generation-scoped availability snapshots index the full selected date once, retain stable-key playable answers across filter-only renders, and rebuild on date/media/day-state renders so filter changes do not repeat expensive media resolution.
A date with zero known playable media is reported as NO_KNOWN_PLAYABLE_MEDIA and is excluded from media-ready p95/max rather than treated as a timeout.
Dates with known database media must reach full known-media readiness within the MEDIA_READY timeout; media-ready p95/max/timeouts are blocking certification metrics.
Efficiency report includes MEDIA_DATES, MEDIA_READY_P95, MEDIA_READY_MAX, MEDIA_READY_TIMEOUTS, MEDIA_KNOWN_GAMES, MEDIA_READY_GAMES, MEDIA_KNOWN_ASSETS, and MEDIA_READY_COVERAGE.
Every tested date line reports day-visible latency and known-media-ready latency/counts separately.

Actual click-to-first-frame playback remains certified by Ultimate Playback; Efficiency Certification measures the prerequisite that already-known playable media is attached and selectable before the click.
Native cold-thin certification omits custom X-SBB headers and credentials so GitHub Pages cross-origin GETs do not trigger unnecessary CORS preflight failures.
tests/test_v4713_media_readiness_runtime.js and tests/test_v4713_media_readiness.py are blocking contracts for media readiness and cold-thin preflight avoidance.
CFB is a first-class persistent American Football competition with stable league id CFB and season id CFB2026; next season resets seasonal state without creating a second permanent main-bar league.

CFB weekly membership is exactly every FBS game with at least one participant in the weekly AP Top 25 snapshot applicable to that ESPN schedule week; ranked-v-ranked games appear once and carry both ranks.
Weekly AP rank snapshots are immutable after first successful persistence; historical games retain that week's rank labels even after subsequent polls change the team's rank or ranked status.
Future CFB weeks are never projected using an older poll. A week is materialized only when its AP Top 25 snapshot exists.
Recent materialized CFB weeks may refresh score/status data, but rank fields are rebuilt only from the already-frozen weekly snapshot.
CFB events carry clean participant names for media matching plus displayName/rank/apRank/rankLabel/rankWeek metadata for archived ranking display.
CFB schedule authority is ESPN FBS scoreboard groups=80; ranking authority is ESPN AP Top 25 rankings.
The operator playlist PLPydJJjt7Pb4 is enrolled as the primary Purple/Extended CFB media source with Full Game Highlights intent.
CFB exposes /api/cfb/status, /api/cfb/rankings, and POST /api/cfb/refresh diagnostics/control endpoints.

CFB is installed through Day State bootstrap and Competition Builder persistence so it participates in backend registry, History, Day State, Statistics, Playlists, Game Center, and dynamic frontend league navigation without a special-event branch.
tests/test_v4714_cfb_ranked_season.py and tests/test_v4714_cfb_ranked_runtime.py are blocking contracts.

Filter-only score-ribbon renders reuse the complete all-league card bank for the selected date and update visibility without reconstructing game cards; stale or incomplete banks fall back to the canonical full render.
The all-league card bank preserves the original score-card DOM nodes and their playback/click handlers; only the filter-specific Silver roundup card may be refreshed during the fast path.

Efficiency Certification records filter fast-path count, card-bank builds, availability-snapshot reuse, filter-apply p95, stabilized DOM baseline/restored counts, DOM peak, and DOM sampling-window spread.
DOM retained growth is measured after state restoration and a stabilization window rather than from a single immediate node count, while peak DOM growth remains diagnostic evidence.
A FAIL grade in any scored efficiency metric cannot be downgraded to PASS by optional-metric aggregation.

tests/test_v4715_efficiency_hardening_runtime.js and tests/test_v4715_efficiency_hardening.py are blocking contracts for filter-node reuse, availability snapshot reuse, media-readiness accounting, and stabilized DOM certification.

Same-day repeat matchups with distinct canonical event IDs are rendered as legitimate doubleheaders and labeled GAME 1 / GAME 2 in chronological scheduled-time order; exact duplicate event IDs are defensively hidden without deleting canonical card nodes.

MLB score-card playback rejects any media asset whose title explicitly names a calendar date different from the score event date, preventing a prior-day game in the same series from satisfying the current game.

Day State revalidates persisted EVENT_MEDIA relationships against the current evidence matcher before exposing compact eventPlans; stale date/team conflicts are removed at the read boundary and counted in mediaSafety diagnostics.

Competition-specific operator playlist metadata preserves titleIncludePhrase, sourceLabel, sourceType, season bounds, and include-all policy through normalization and curated crawler conversion.

tests/test_v4716_ribbon_identity_runtime.js and tests/test_v4716_ribbon_identity_playlist.py are blocking contracts for doubleheader identity, explicit MLB title-date safety, Day State stale-media revalidation, and CFB playlist enforcement.

A single physical YouTube/direct media asset cannot satisfy multiple canonical games on the same date unless provider event/game identity proves one unique owner; ambiguous doubleheader media is removed from every unresolved event plan until correctly associated.
CFB Game Center resolves the selected ESPN college-football event through the shared normalized Game Center contract and preserves the AP Top 25 score identity.
Game Center displays a top linescore for MLB by inning plus R/H/E, NFL/CFB/NBA by quarter plus total, and NHL by period plus total when provider period data is available.
ESPN win probability is normalized into the Game Center read model and displayed only when the provider supplies win-probability samples; its absence never blocks Game Center.

Historical GAME media whose normalized database validation_state is VERIFIED, whose runtime_state is not FAILED, and which has a playable YouTube/direct transport hydrates as verifiedPlayable even when legacy asset_json omitted that flag.
A historical date such as May 13 must prefer already-assigned verified database media before advertising FIND/search for the same canonical game.

tier2.name: Extended Soak
requirements: At least 90% of expected 15-second telemetry samples are captured across the full soak window
No telemetry gap exceeds 2.5 sample intervals
Playback currentTime advances while state is playing; sustained no-progress beyond 45 seconds fails
Native video play-request acknowledgment is bounded so a pending HTMLMediaElement.play() Promise cannot delay first-frame recovery
Sustained buffering beyond 45 seconds fails
Timed-out game-transition calls are evidence and must recover within 20 seconds; only unrecovered transition timeouts fail the soak
Media decode/provider failures must self-recover to another playable selection rather than strand unattended playback
No playback ownership invariant violation
No same-media currentTime restart or same-media reselection regression
Game Center remains tied to game-scoped active media
Workers remain healthy during periodic platform snapshots
No milestone clean-window errors
No excessive JavaScript heap growth when browser heap telemetry is available

tier3.name: Controlled Chaos / Recovery
requirements: Background rerank storm preserves active playback
Aborted concurrent request storm recovers
Expected invalid-route failure is isolated from playback
Standby-player disruption does not disturb active playback
Resource-mode turbulence restores the original mode
Repeated game transitions preserve Game Center ownership
Manual pause survives concurrent API pressure
Post-chaos clean recovery window is healthy
Game Center provider 429 opens a bounded scheduler circuit and cancels queued background amplification
Tier 3 chaos evidence remains exportable through the post-chaos recovery reset
Timing-only WARN evidence remains visible and advisory; only failed assertions or failed recovery gates block Tier 3 certification
